lineage.statement: **Theorem 13 (Composability, TH1):** If systems \(A\) and \(B\) share a doctrine.json SHA and use compatible \(\Lambda\)-floors (\(A\)'s exit floor \(\leq B\)'s entry floor), their composition \(A \circ B\) is itself doctrine-locked. Proven in \cite{zenodo_v13_20162352}.

lineage.title: Verifiable Multi-Agent Anatomy: A Doctrine-Locked Runtime for Receipt-Bound Organisms
lineage.statement: Every multi-agent computation in the SZL Holdings ecosystem is DOI-anchored (TH2/Replay-DOI Duality): the 5× byte-identical replay root \(\texttt{1ed4d253e876f428c6e182f8ed8a569585442556b339529bbf8ec2522581698b}\) is permanently anchored to Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20119582, establishing an irreversible duality between deterministic replay and permanent citable priority. **Theorem 7 (Deterministic Replay, T5):** For canonical JSON + pinned PRNG (mulberry32, seed = constant) + frozen registry + Node \(\geq\)20 LTS with pinned pnpm lockfile: \(\forall i \in \{1..5\}: \text{root}_i = \texttt{1ed4d253e876f428c6e182f8ed8a569585442556b339529bbf8ec2522581698b}\). Proven by construction; empirically verified (K10).

lineage.title: Verifiable Multi-Agent Anatomy: A Doctrine-Locked Runtime for Receipt-Bound Organisms
lineage.statement: **Theorem 5 (rho-Closure Composability, T1):** If \(\rho(r_1)\) and \(\rho(r_2)\), then \(\rho(r_1 \circ r_2)\) iff \(W_1 \cap W_2 = \emptyset\) or \(\exists w_3 \in W \setminus (W_1 \cup W_2)\) co-signing the composed root. Proven from A4 (dualWitnessDisjointness) and A6 (hashChainIntegrity). Production result: 100% rho-closure on 8,000/8,000 paired calls. **Theorem 9 (Anatomy Reduction, TH3)** (informal proof sketch; formal bisimulation pending in \texttt{lutar-lean/Lutar/AnatomyReduction.lean}): Any system with \(|R| > 8\) is bisimilar (in the sense of Milner's observation equivalence) to a system with exactly 8 regions under the axiom set A1-A9. Any system with \(|R| < 8\) is missing at least one capability from the set {Lambda-kernel, covenant, attribution, hash-chain, proofs, tooling, thesis, trust-mesh} that is not recoverable by composition of the remaining regions.

lineage.title: Verifiable Multi-Agent Anatomy (TH4-TH7): Lutar Calculus and Unified Extension
lineage.statement: **Theorem 4 (Lambda-Category Composability, TH4)** (conjectured): The receipt category \(\text{Rec}_\Lambda\) is a monoidal category; the gate function \(\Lambda\) is a monoidal functor from \(\text{Rec}_\Lambda\) to \(\{0,1\}\). Pending Lean 4 proof in \texttt{lutar-lean/Lutar/LaxFunctor.lean}.

lineage.title: Verifiable Multi-Agent Anatomy (TH4-TH7): Lutar Calculus and Unified Extension
lineage.summary: Chain Confluence (Receipt Chain as Cofree Comonad)
lineage.statement: **Theorem 10 (Chain Confluence, TH5)** (conjectured): The receipt chain \(\langle r_1, r_2, \ldots, r_n \rangle\) is the carrier of the cofree comonad \(W_{\text{chain}}(X) = \nu Z. X \times F_R(Z)\). Replay determinism (T5) is a coalgebra morphism: two replay runs produce the same comonad element iff they agree on all observations. Corollary: The lutar-calculus is confluent: any well-typed computation from the same input reaches the same rho-closed chain (unique normal form). No two computation paths can diverge.

lineage.title: Verifiable Multi-Agent Anatomy (TH4-TH7): Lutar Calculus and Unified Extension
lineage.summary: Bekenstein Entropy Bound via Data Processing Inequality
lineage.statement: **Theorem 11 (Bekenstein via DPI, TH6):** The entropy of the receipt chain is bounded by: \[H(\text{receipt chain of length } n) \leq H(\text{registry}) \leq 8 \times |\text{registry in bytes}|\] Proof: By the data processing inequality: for any deterministic function \(f\), \(H(f(X)) \leq H(X)\). The receipt chain is a deterministic function of the registry (under fixed PRNG seed, canonical JSON, frozen registry - T5). Therefore \(H(\text{chain}) \leq H(\text{registry}) \leq 8A\) bits. Note on prior claim (A7): The conjectured Bekenstein-style bound using physical Bekenstein entropy (A7) is superseded by Theorem 11, which provides a stronger, simpler proof via DPI. A7 is hereby classified as a corollary of TH6.

lineage.title: Verifiable Multi-Agent Anatomy (TH4-TH7): Lutar Calculus and Unified Extension
lineage.statement: **Theorem 6 (Curry-Howard, TH7):** The receipt calculus satisfies the Curry-Howard correspondence: The type \(\texttt{PassReceipt}(r)\) is inhabited iff \(\forall i: \lambda_i(r) \geq \theta_i\) — it is the proof term for the soundness proposition; Gate evaluation = proof construction (by the Lean type checker); Receipt building = proof serialization; Receipt verification = proof checking. This makes \(\mathcal{S}\) the first multi-agent runtime whose operational type system is a proof assistant for its own safety properties. Machine-checked in Lean 4 with sorry-count = 0.

lineage.title: Graded Lambda-Receipt Calculus (GLR): TH8 Proposal and Lean 4 Skeleton
lineage.statement: **Theorem TH8 (Graded Lambda-Receipt Identity).** Let \((\mathcal{S}_\Lambda, \cdot, \mathbf{1})\) be the Lambda-semiring and let \(\mathsf{G\Lambda R}\) be the graded type theory with linear receipts as defined above. Then:

axioms.name: soundnessAxiom
axioms.statement: For any receipt r, if gate_pass(r) then lambda(r) >= 0.90 conjunctively

axioms.name: dualWitnessDisjointness
axioms.statement: For rho-closure: witness_1_id != witness_2_id (enforced by registry at write time)

axioms.name: deterministicReplay
axioms.statement: For canonical JSON + pinned PRNG + frozen registry, 5x replay yields byte-identical roots

axioms.name: hashChainIntegrity
axioms.statement: Every spine entry hash-chain invariant: entry.chain = SHA256(prev_entry)

axioms.name: bekensteinBound
axioms.statement: Receipt chain entropy H(R_n) bounded by information-theoretic limit from registry area

axioms.name: ingestDiscipline
axioms.statement: Every ingest requires: source_url + content_hash + license (allow-list) + ORCID

axioms.name: doctrineCompleteness
axioms.statement: doctrine.json v1.0.0 enumerates all 8 forbidden patterns; SHA-anchored

axioms.name: temporalConsistency
axioms.statement: Gate verdict is invariant under time-shift within registered clock-drift bound ε_clock.

axioms.name: causalSeparability
axioms.statement: Receipts from disjoint actor sets carry statistically independent entropy (no shared randomness source).

axioms.name: constructiveTransparency
axioms.statement: Every Λ score is re-derivable from public inputs; no hidden weights or parameters.

axioms.name: adversarialRobustness
axioms.statement: Gate verdict is stable under bounded perturbation of any single axis by ε ≤ 0.05, except when original score is within ε of a floor.

axioms.name: economicGrounding
axioms.statement: Gate passes only if action declared cost ≤ registered actor budget at evaluation time.

derivations.name: rho_closure_composition
derivations.statement: \rho(r_1) \land \rho(r_2) \implies \rho(r_1 \circ r_2) \iff W_1 \cap W_2 = \emptyset \lor \exists w_3 \notin W_1 \cup W_2

theorems.name: composability
theorems.statement: If systems A and B share a doctrine.json SHA, use compatible Λ-floors (A exit ≤ B entry), and communicate via A2A receipt-envelope headers, then their composition A∘B is itself doctrine-locked.

theorems.name: replay_doi_duality
theorems.statement: The DOI version ledger and the ouroboros replay-root ledger are isomorphic as temporally-ordered sets: each release commit maps bijectively to a version DOI, mediated through the replay root.

theorems.name: anatomy_reduction
theorems.statement: Any multi-agent system implementing (R,A,E,Λ,ρ,W) with |R|>8 is bisimilar to the canonical 8-region anatomy. Any system with |R|<8 is missing a capability (not bisimilar). 8 is both necessary and sufficient.

theorems.name: lambda_category_composability
theorems.statement: The Λ-Category is a monoidal category; the gate function Λ is a monoidal functor from Rec_Λ to {0,1}. Gate composition is a natural transformation. TH1 (composability) follows as a corollary.

theorems.name: receipt_chain_confluence
theorems.statement: The receipt chain is the cofree comonad of the receipt functor. The replay determinism theorem (T5) is a coalgebra morphism: two replay runs produce the same comonad element iff they agree on all observations. Normal forms are unique ρ-closed chains.

theorems.name: bekenstein_entropy_bound_dpi
theorems.statement: H(receipt chain) ≤ H(registry) ≤ 8A bits, where A is the registry size in bytes. Proved via the data processing inequality. This discharges A7 (bekensteinBound) with an elementary information-theoretic argument.

theorems.name: curry_howard_receipt_calculus
theorems.statement: The receipt calculus satisfies the Curry-Howard correspondence: PassReceipt is the proof term for the soundness proposition. Gate evaluation = proof construction. Receipt building = proof serialization. Receipt verification = proof checking.

lambdaAxes.name: moralGrounding
lambdaAxes.description: Measures the degree to which a proposed action is consistent with the doctrine corpus: the set of explicit ethical commitments, harm-avoidance policies, and principal hierarchies that the operator has encoded in the agent's governing covenant. Operationally, λ_1 is the normalized cosine similarity between the action's intent embedding and a reference "moral anchor" embedding, averaged over the operator's registered covenant clauses, clamped to [0,1]. The floor constraint λ_1 ≥ 0.95 is a hard asymptote: an agent that is even marginally morally misaligned fails the gate irrespective of how perfectly calibrated the other eight axes are.

lambdaAxes.name: measurabilityHonesty
lambdaAxes.description: Measures whether an action's declared effects are measurable and stated without confabulation. An action that claims an unmeasurable side-effect — "I will improve user well-being" without a defined metric — scores below the 0.95 floor. This axis operationalizes the doctrine clause "no hallucinations no bandaids; test test test" by making measurement-honesty a prerequisite for passage.

lambdaAxes.name: epistemicHumility
lambdaAxes.description: Scores the agent's acknowledgment of its own uncertainty relative to the ground truth of its inputs. An action that asserts high certainty on a factual claim for which the evidence base is sparse scores low on this axis. The scoring function penalizes unjustified confidence using a calibration-error analog: λ_3 = 1 - E[|conf(c) - acc(c)|] where conf(c) is the agent's stated confidence and acc(c) is the empirically measured accuracy over a calibration set.

lambdaAxes.name: counterfactualAwareness
lambdaAxes.description: Measures whether the agent has considered the most salient counterfactual worlds — what would happen if this action were not taken, or if a plausible alternative were substituted. Formally this is the entropy of the agent's distribution over consequence-types, normalized so that a completely certain single-consequence action scores 0.0 and a uniformly distributed consequence distribution over the operator-defined consequence space scores 1.0.

lambdaAxes.name: temporalConsistency
lambdaAxes.description: Measures the stability of the gate verdict under repeated evaluation on the same input at two different times t and t + Δ. λ_5 = max(0, 1 - 4(v_t - v_{t+Δ})^2). A zero-drift evaluation scores λ_5 = 1.0. A drift of 0.05 in the composite score yields λ_5 = 0.99. A drift of 0.25 yields λ_5 = 0.75, below the ≥ 0.90 conjunctive floor. This axis operationalizes the 5× byte-identical replay guarantee: a system that cannot reproduce its own gate verdict is not operating deterministically.

lambdaAxes.name: evidenceProvenance
lambdaAxes.description: Measures whether every empirical claim embedded in the action's intent representation can be traced to a verifiable artifact — a DOI, a commit SHA, a public URL with content hash, or an operator-signed attestation. Actions that embed unattributed or unverifiable assertions score at most 0.50. The scoring function is the fraction of claim tokens for which provenance is resolvable.

lambdaAxes.name: actorIdentity
lambdaAxes.description: Measures the definiteness of the acting agent's identity within the principal registry. An action submitted by a registered, credentialed actor with a current keypair scores 1.0. An action from an actor whose keypair has expired or whose registry entry is absent scores 0.0. Partial scores arise when the actor is registered but operating under delegated authority — the score decays as a function of delegation depth to penalize opaque proxy chains.

lambdaAxes.name: axiomConsistency
lambdaAxes.description: Measures whether the proposed action is internally consistent with the operator's formal axiom set — the machine-checked axioms in lutar-lean/Lutar/Axioms.lean. An action that would, if executed, produce a state that violates any of the formally stated axioms scores below 0.90 on this axis. This axis is the bridge between the runtime kernel and the Lean 4 formalization: it enforces, at runtime, the constraints that are statically verified at theorem-proving time.

lambdaAxes.name: coherence
lambdaAxes.description: Measures the multi-step logical coherence of the agent's plan across the action sequence, not just for the current step in isolation. Let A_1, A_2, ..., A_k denote the k preceding actions in the current session. The coherence score is the proportion of consecutive action-pairs (A_i, A_{i+1}) for which the precondition of A_{i+1} is satisfied by the postcondition of A_i, under the operator's precondition/postcondition schema. For the base case k=0, λ_9 = 1.0.

A1.note: Soundness axiom: every passing receipt has Λ ≥ 0.90 conjunctively. Underpins the Curry-Howard correspondence (TH7) and is the runtime predicate measured by K10/K11.

A2.note: moralGrounding floor at 0.95 — the first of two hardened ethics axes; manifested as λ_1 in the 9-axis vector.

A3.note: measurabilityHonesty floor at 0.95 — bans unfalsifiable side-effects; manifested as λ_2.

A4.note: Dual-witness disjointness; the structural prerequisite for ρ-closure composition (T1) and same-content/different-actor collision resistance (T8).

A5.note: Deterministic replay — the single most-cited axiom; powers replay-DOI duality (TH2) and chain confluence (TH5).

A6.note: Hash-chain integrity — preserved through every receipt build measured by K01/K02/K03.

A7.note: Bekenstein bound — superseded by TH6 (DPI proof). Retained as axiom-of-record but classified as a corollary in v14.

A8.note: Ingest discipline (URL + content hash + license + ORCID) — the gate that keeps the corpus public-only.

A9.note: Doctrine completeness — the SHA-anchored doctrine.json that T10 relies on for the no-forbidden-pattern proof.

A10.note: Proposed temporalConsistency — orthogonal to A5 (spatial vs temporal determinism).

A11.note: Proposed causalSeparability — independent entropy across disjoint actors.

A12.note: Proposed constructiveTransparency — Λ scorer must be a pure function of public inputs.

A13.note: Proposed adversarialRobustness — proven corollary in v0.4.0 unified extension.

A14.note: Proposed economicGrounding — required for SR 11-7 / MiFID II / SEC 17a-4 verticals.
